methodology: Every insight cites the specific ratio/period pair it is derived from in ratios_timeseries.json.

risk_signals.statement: FY2017 was the only loss-making year in the researched series: EPS -0.28, ROA -0.08%, ROE -1.15%, a sharp reversal from FY2016's already-weak 5.31% ROE. The bank recovered strongly the following year (ROE 12.51% in FY2018), suggesting a discrete, one-year event rather than sustained distress.

Total assets grew from BDT 285.5bn (FY2015) to BDT 981.2bn (FY2024), a 3.4x increase, with ROE recovering from the FY2017 loss to a series-high 12.53% in FY2022 before profitability detail became unavailable for FY2023-2024 due to source extraction gaps.

The 'sustained_growth_and_recovery' signal above called FY2022's 12.53% ROE a 'series-high' — that was true only of the FY2015-2024 window available at the time. With FY2011-2014 now backfilled, FY2011 shows a higher ROE of 18.17% (PAT 3,140.22m on a much smaller 157.2bn balance sheet), followed by a sharp fall to 9.37% in FY2012 alongside NPL more than doubling (2.02% to 5.05%) as the loan book grew and matured. The true series-high ROE across all primary-sourced years (2011-2024) is FY2011's 18.17%, not FY2022's 12.53%.

Backfilling FY2011-2014 surfaced two source-document data-quality issues, both resolved and fully documented in sources.json: (1) the FY2012 and FY2013 annual reports' own summary tables mislabel pre-provision operating profit as 'Pre-tax Profit' (e.g. showing 6,135.80m for FY2012 against an actual post-provision profit-before-tax of 4,317.08m) — proven via an exact match to the FY2014 report's own Value Added Statement tax reconciliation for FY2013 and FY2014, and via tax-rate implausibility (an impossible 71.3% effective rate) for FY2012. (2) FY2011's reported CAR of 11.56% does not reconcile with the same table's own actual-capital/RWA figures (17,976.71/132,581.60 = 13.56%), a ~2 percentage-point discrepancy left unresolved and flagged rather than silently corrected, since — unlike the profit mislabeling — no independent third source was available to determine which single figure in that column is wrong.

Reported NPL at Pubali Bank rose from 2.02% (FY2011) to a series-high 6.25% (FY2014), then improved to 4.38% (FY2019, the most recent year with a directly reported NPL% in this dataset before FY2025). Press coverage puts FY2025 NPL at 2.20%, notably better than the sector-wide FY2024 medians described elsewhere in this project's cross-bank analysis (median NPL 9.55%). Treat this apparent improvement cautiously: FY2020-2024 NPL is not available in this dataset (see data_gaps) so the trajectory between FY2019's 4.38% and FY2025's press-reported 2.20% is unobserved, and the FY2025 figure itself is secondary-sourced, not read from a primary report.

New Q1-Q3 backfill (sourced from the FY2018 Annual Report's own 'Evaluation of the Quarterly Financials' comparative column, since FY2017's own version of this table is OCR-corrupted) refines the existing 'fy2017_net_loss' signal: FY2017 was NOT a weak year throughout. Cumulative Net Profit After Tax rose monotonically through the first nine months (494.66m at Q1, 878.00m at Q2, 1,188.70m at Q3, on a cumulative EPS path of 0.52/0.88/1.19), and cumulative pre-provision operating profit reached 8,184.9m for the full year (also monotonically increasing every quarter, per the 'Total operating income (A)' and 'Total operating expenses (B)' rows of the same source table) -- yet the audited full year closed at a NET LOSS (EPS -0.28, already in 2017_Q4.json). This implies a discrete Q4-2017 net loss of approximately -1,469.9m taka, corroborated by the equity roll-forward in the same table (Sep17 25,878.77m -> Dec17 24,420.31m, a ~1,458m Q4 decline). Because pre-provision profit stayed positive and rising throughout, the loss originated below the operating-profit line -- i.e. a large Q4 loan-loss provisioning and/or tax charge -- not from a revenue or net-interest-margin collapse. This distinction (a sudden, large, late-year provisioning shock hitting an otherwise-normal, profitable year) was not visible in the Q4-only dataset and should replace any reading of FY2017 as a year of gradually deteriorating performance.

New Q1-Q3 backfill surfaces a previously-invisible FY2019 pattern, smaller than FY2017's but the same shape: cumulative Net Profit After Tax rose from 734.60m (Q1) to 2,034.21m (Q2) to a peak of 2,570.68m (Q3, cumulative EPS 2.50), then FELL to 2,143.27m for the full year (EPS 2.10, per the existing 2019_Q4.json) -- a discrete Q4-2019 net loss of approximately -427.4m taka. This is corroborated by the equity roll-forward in the same source table (Sep19 28,954.66m -> Dec19 28,552.84m, a ~401.8m Q4 decline, consistent in sign and rough magnitude). Unlike FY2017, this Q4 dip is modest and does not flip the full year negative, but it is a second, independent instance in this bank's series of Q4 (audit-period) charges materially reducing an otherwise-solid 9-month run rate -- worth watching for a recurring pattern (possible year-end provisioning discipline) rather than treating each occurrence as a one-off.

New Q1-Q3 backfill (DSE company-page interim table via Wayback Machine, 2026-08-27) surfaced a recurring, well-evidenced mechanical pattern: Pubali Bank's AGM consistently falls Mar-Jun, i.e. BETWEEN Q1 and Q2 of the same calendar year. In years where that AGM declares a bonus/stock share dividend, Q1's own EPS is computed on the PRE-bonus share count (as filed before the AGM) while Q2 and the Half-Yearly cumulative figure use the POST-bonus count, without retroactively restating Q1 -- so Q1(discrete)+Q2(discrete) does not sum to the reported Half-Yearly EPS in those years. Confirmed with clean share-count arithmetic in FY2011 (24/04/2011 AGM, 35% bonus for FY2010: Q1 EPS 0.92 implies ~496.86m pre-bonus shares = 670,761,000/1.35 almost exactly; Q2/Q3 reconcile against the new 670.76m count) and FY2014 (25/03/2014 AGM, 5% bonus for FY2013: Q1 reconciles to the old 838.45m count, Q2/Q3 to the new 880.37m count), and recurs with a small (0.18-0.28 BDT/share) Q1+Q2-vs-HY gap in FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 (three consecutive years, each with rising paid-up capital consistent with an annual bonus issue: 1,156.83m to 1,301.43m to 1,561.72m shares outstanding). Years with a cash-only AGM dividend (FY2013, FY2015, FY2016) show exact Q1+Q2=HY reconciliation instead, confirming the mechanism rather than a general data-quality problem with the source. FY2012 is a partial exception where Q1's EPS does not reconcile against any independently known share count -- recorded as reported, cause not resolved. This pattern was invisible in the previously-available FY2017-2020 embedded-table data (which is presented purely cumulative, with no discrete Q2/Q3 breakout to expose the discontinuity) and should inform how any downstream user interprets a same-year Q1-vs-Q2/HY EPS comparison for this bank.

FY2025 is the only year in this series NOT sourced from the bank's own annual report text: pubalibangla.com is now behind a Cloudflare bot-challenge that blocked every retrieval method available this session (direct fetch under multiple user agents, a reader proxy, and Wayback Machine's live-capture trigger, which itself returned HTTP 520). FY2025 figures instead come from press coverage of the bank's AGM-approved results (total assets 1,180,136.6m, deposits 895,194.9m, loans/advances 711,406.3m, PAT 10,795.6m, EPS 8.30, NPL 2.20%, ROE 15.51%, CAR 15.34%) plus a third-party aggregator (stockanalysis.com) for total_liabilities/total_equity (70,695m) only, which is not reconcilable against the press total_assets figure (0.29% gap) and was separately observed to differ from this dataset's own FY2023/FY2024 primary-sourced figures by 0.04-4.8% on comparable line items in those years. The 35.1% YoY equity growth this produces in ratios_timeseries.json for FY2025 is at least partly a source-switching artifact (FY2024's equity is primary-sourced, FY2025's is aggregator-sourced) and should not be read as a confirmed economic result without primary-source verification.

historical_context: Pubali Bank's now-15-year researched series (FY2011-2025; FY2025 secondary-sourced, see below) opens with a high-ROE period (18.17% in FY2011, the series high) that gives way to a multi-year decline as the loan book roughly doubled and NPL rose from 2.02% to 6.25% (FY2011-2014), then a single sharp loss-making year in FY2017 (EPS -0.28, ROE -1.15%, the only loss in the series) with a strong one-year recovery (ROE 12.51% in FY2018) and a further multi-year climb to 12.53% ROE in FY2022. Total assets grew from BDT 157.2bn (FY2011) to a press-reported BDT 1,180.1bn (FY2025), roughly 7.5x over 14 years. Data depth is uneven across the series: FY2011-2022 has full ratio detail (cross-validated extensively during the FY2011-2014 backfill, including an exact Value Added Statement tax reconciliation for FY2013-2014); FY2023-2024 have balance-sheet aggregates only, from unusually short/partial source-text extracts (likely an artifact of how the archive was built by a parallel session, not a reflection of the bank's actual reporting); and FY2025 is sourced from press coverage rather than the bank's own report because pubalibangla.com is now Cloudflare-protected. The FY2020-2025 profitability and asset-quality trajectory is therefore only partially observed within this dataset despite the calendar years being nominally covered.
data_gaps: UPDATED 2026-08-27: Q1/Q2/Q3 (unaudited interim) data is available for FY2017-2020 from a BSEC-mandated data table ('Evaluation of the Quarterly Financials by the Audit Committee and by the Board') embedded in those four years' own annual reports -- all 14 available annual report texts (FY2011-2024) were searched and this table was confirmed present only in FY2017-2020, and this specific method (the bank's own annual reports) is exhausted for the other 10 years. A SEPARATE technique -- DSE's own dsebd.org company page's live 'Interim Financial Performance' table, reconstructed historically via Wayback Machine captures of that same URL (the method already proven on RUPALIBANK) -- has now ALSO recovered Q1/Q2/Q3 (thinner, EPS/turnover/price-level only, no balance sheet) for FY2011, FY2012, FY2013, FY2014, FY2015, FY2016, FY2021, FY2023, FY2024 (Q1/Q2 clean, Q3 discrete EPS specifically not disclosed by the source), FY2025 (Q1/Q2 only -- Q3 had not occurred/was not yet capturable as of the latest usable capture) and, as a bonus beyond this dataset's normal target range, FY2026 Q1/Q2 via a live fetch. FY2022 Q1/Q3 remains a CONFIRMED gap by this method too -- no Wayback capture with HTTP 200 exists anywhere in 2022 (the only two captures return HTTP 403/302), and DSE's separate Auditors_opinion PDF repository (checked directly per the same technique memo) has no PUBALIBANK entry for any year (most likely because that repository is for qualified/adverse audit opinions, which this bank does not have) -- FY2022 is the only fully-unrecoverable Q1-Q3 year left in this series. See sources.json for the full per-year sourcing and the newly-discovered AGM/bonus-share-timing pattern that explains a recurring small Q1-vs-Half-Yearly EPS reconciliation gap in FY2024-2026 (also documented as a risk_signal above). Within the FY2017-2020 window (the richer, balance-sheet-bearing source), FY2020's own table is itself a partial extraction (roughly half its rows missing, likely a PDF-layout artifact) -- Investments, Balance-with-other-banks, Fixed Assets, Subordinated Bond, Other Liabilities, Off-Balance-Sheet Items, Total Operating Income and Profit-before-provision are not available for FY2020's three quarters, and its total_assets/total_equity are derived via a balance-sheet identity rather than directly reported (see 2020_Q1/Q2/Q3.json period_notes). NPL ratio is available for FY2011-2014, FY2018-2019, and FY2025 (press-sourced) but NOT for FY2015-2017 or FY2020-2024 (7 of 15 years) -- note this gap is about the ANNUAL NPL%, which the new Q1-Q3 table does not report either (it discloses balance-sheet and income-statement figures only, no asset-quality ratios). CAR is available for FY2011-2014, FY2019, and FY2025 (press-sourced) but NOT for FY2015-2018 or FY2020-2024 (9 of 15 years). FY2023-2024 have balance-sheet aggregates only (no income statement, EPS, ROA/ROE, NPL, or CAR) due to partial/corrupted source-text extracts for those two years' reports — re-extracting those two PDFs directly would be a natural next step to close this gap (the local .txt files predate the site's current Cloudflare protection, but the PDFs themselves would need to be re-fetched, which is now blocked). FY2025 has no primary source at all (see sources.json for the full attempt log); a future session with real-browser access, or a later Wayback crawl of the live FY2025 PDF URL, should re-extract it and reconcile the several small unresolved cross-source discrepancies noted in 2025_Q4.json's period_note. FY2011's car_pct has an internal ~2 percentage-point inconsistency versus its own table's actual-capital/RWA figures, left unresolved (see sources.json).
